title: Commit or Ignore Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js drag-and-drop sorting activity. Students place ten robot project files into a Commit to git bin or an Add to .gitignore bin, get a check or an X with a one-sentence reason after every drop, and watch a live .gitignore preview build from their choices.

educational.topic: Version control hygiene: config, secrets, and .gitignore
learningObjectives: Classify project files as belonging in version control or in .gitignore
Explain why secrets.py must never be committed and why a committed secret stays in git history
Explain why rebuilt files such as __pycache__/ and *.pyc are ignored
Explain why config.py, libraries, README.md, and .gitignore itself are committed
prerequisites: Config, secrets, and .gitignore file patterns from Chapter 10

controls.label: File cards
controls.purpose: Move a file into the Commit to git bin, the Add to .gitignore bin, or back to the pile

controls.label: Commit selected
controls.purpose: Keyboard-friendly way to place the selected card in the commit bin

controls.label: Add selected to .gitignore
controls.purpose: Keyboard-friendly way to place the selected card in the ignore bin

controls.label: Check All
controls.purpose: Color every sorted card and summarize right, wrong, and unsorted

controls.label: Show Answers
controls.purpose: Move every card to its correct bin

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return all cards to the pile

controls.label: Up/Down, C, I
controls.purpose: Select a card and place it without a mouse

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Drag-and-drop sorting into two bins with a live .gitignore preview
keyQuestions: Which file holds your WiFi password, and what happens if you commit it?
Why do we ignore __pycache__/ and *.pyc files?
Why is it safe to commit config.py?
Why should the .gitignore file itself be committed?
commonMisconceptions: Adding a file to .gitignore after committing it removes it from history
config.py is secret because it contains numbers
Library files like lib/vl53l0x.py do not need to be committed because they are not your code
assessmentOpportunities: Score of 10 out of 10 with written reasons
Grouping ignored files by reason (secret, rebuilt, operating-system clutter)
Exit ticket about a secret that was already committed
